## Appendix D — Interactive Dashboard: Chess Performance Analytics

> **Objective:**  
> Provide a single interactive interface that allows exploration of:
> - Rating distributions (FIDE vs Lichess)  
> - Player win-rate trends  
> - Time-series rating progressions  
> - Growth-model parameters (linear + nonlinear)  

---

### D.1 Setup and Required Packages

```{r dashboard-setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Install once if not already
install.packages(c("flexdashboard", "plotly", "DT", "broom", "here", "minpack.lm", "lme4", "zoo"))

library(flexdashboard)
library(plotly)
library(DT)
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
library(lubridate)
library(minpack.lm) # for nlsLM
library(lme4)
library(zoo)
```

---

### D.2 Load Data

```{r load-data, message=FALSE}
summary_path <- "../../data/player_summary.csv"
lichess_path <- "../../data/lichess_clean.csv"
rating_hist_path <- "../../data/lichess_rating_history.csv"

player_summary <- read_csv(summary_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
lichess_clean <- read_csv(lichess_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
rating_history <- read_csv(rating_hist_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Preview data structures
glimpse(player_summary)
glimpse(lichess_clean)
glimpse(rating_history)
```

---

### D.3 Interactive Rating Distribution Comparison

```{r rating-distribution, fig.height=6, fig.width=9}
# Prepare long format for FIDE vs Lichess comparison
rating_comparison <- player_summary %>%
  select(rating_group, fide_avg_rating_standard, lichess_avg_rating) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(fide_avg_rating_standard, lichess_avg_rating),
    names_to = "source",
    values_to = "rating"
  ) %>%
  mutate(source = recode(source,
    fide_avg_rating_standard = "FIDE (Standard)",
    lichess_avg_rating = "Lichess (Online)"
  ))

# Create interactive plotly chart
p1 <- ggplot(rating_comparison, aes(x = rating_group, y = rating, fill = source, 
                                     text = paste0("Rating: ", round(rating, 0), 
                                                  "<br>Group: ", rating_group,
                                                  "<br>Source: ", source))) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2E86AB", "#E67E22")) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Player Ratings: FIDE vs Lichess",
    x = "Rating Group",
    y = "Average Rating",
    fill = "Data Source"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

ggplotly(p1, tooltip = "text")
```

---

### D.4 Win Rate Analysis by Rating Tier

```{r winrate-interactive, fig.height=5, fig.width=9}
p2 <- ggplot(player_summary, aes(x = rating_group, y = lichess_avg_win_rate,
                                  text = paste0("Win Rate: ", 
                                               scales::percent(lichess_avg_win_rate, accuracy = 0.1),
                                               "<br>Group: ", rating_group))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#16A085", width = 0.6, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Win Rate by Rating Group (Lichess)",
    x = "Rating Group",
    y = "Average Win Rate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

ggplotly(p2, tooltip = "text")
```

---

### D.5 Time-Series Rating Progression (Sample Users)

```{r rating-timeseries, fig.height=6, fig.width=10}
# Select top 5 users with most rating history
top_users <- rating_history %>%
  count(user, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5) %>%
  pull(user)

rating_ts_data <- rating_history %>%
  filter(user %in% top_users, category == "Blitz") %>%
  group_by(user) %>%
  mutate(rating_smooth = zoo::rollmean(rating, k = 3, fill = NA, align = "right")) %>%
  ungroup()

p3 <- ggplot(rating_ts_data, aes(x = date, y = rating_smooth, color = user,
                                  text = paste0("User: ", user,
                                               "<br>Date: ", date,
                                               "<br>Rating: ", round(rating_smooth, 0)))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "Rating Progression Over Time (Blitz, Top 5 Active Users)",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Smoothed Rating",
    color = "User"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

ggplotly(p3, tooltip = "text")
```

### D.6 Player Summary Table (Interactive)

```{r summary-table}
# Create interactive data table
player_summary %>%
  select(rating_group, fide_avg_rating_standard, lichess_avg_rating, 
         lichess_avg_win_rate, rating_gap_standard, 
         lichess_players, fide_players) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), round, 2)) %>%
  datatable(
    caption = "Player Summary Statistics: FIDE vs Lichess Comparison",
    colnames = c("Rating Group", "FIDE Avg", "Lichess Avg", "Win Rate", 
                 "Rating Gap", "Lichess N", "FIDE N"),
    filter = "top",
    options = list(
      pageLength = 10,
      scrollX = TRUE,
      dom = 'Bfrtip',
      buttons = c('copy', 'csv', 'excel')
    )
  )
```

### D.7 Nonlinear Growth Model Parameters

```{r growth-parameters, message=FALSE}
# Fit exponential growth models for sample users
rating_nl_df <- rating_history %>%
  filter(category == "Blitz", !is.na(rating)) %>%
  group_by(user) %>%
  mutate(time_index = row_number()) %>%
  filter(n() >= 15) %>%
  ungroup()

target_users <- rating_nl_df %>%
  count(user) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5) %>%
  pull(user)

fit_growth_curve <- function(df) {
  tryCatch({
    model <- nlsLM(
      rating ~ A - B * exp(-k * time_index),
      data = df,
      start = list(A = max(df$rating), B = max(df$rating) - min(df$rating), k = 0.05),
      control = nls.lm.control(maxiter = 100)
    )
    tidy(model) %>% mutate(user = unique(df$user))
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
}

nonlinear_models <- rating_nl_df %>%
  filter(user %in% target_users) %>%
  group_by(user) %>%
  group_modify(~ fit_growth_curve(.x)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Create summary table
growth_summary <- nonlinear_models %>%
  select(user, term, estimate) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = term, values_from = estimate) %>%
  mutate(
    ceiling_rating = round(A, 1),
    learning_rate = round(k, 4),
    rating_span = round(B, 1)
  ) %>%
  select(user, ceiling_rating, learning_rate, rating_span)

datatable(
  growth_summary,
  caption = "Nonlinear Growth Model Parameters (Exponential Fit)",
  colnames = c("User", "Ceiling Rating", "Learning Rate (k)", "Rating Span"),
  options = list(pageLength = 5)
)
```

---

### D.8 Fitted Growth Curves Visualization

```{r growth-curves, fig.height=6, fig.width=10}
predicted_curves <- nonlinear_models %>%
  select(user, term, estimate) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = term, values_from = estimate) %>%
  left_join(rating_nl_df %>% filter(user %in% target_users), by = "user") %>%
  mutate(predicted = A - B * exp(-k * time_index))

# Add tooltip column to data
predicted_curves <- predicted_curves %>%
  mutate(
    tooltip_actual = paste0("User: ", user, "<br>Game: ", time_index, "<br>Actual: ", round(rating, 0)),
    tooltip_pred = paste0("User: ", user, "<br>Game: ", time_index, "<br>Predicted: ", round(predicted, 0))
  )

p4 <- ggplot(predicted_curves, aes(x = time_index, y = rating, color = user)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = predicted), linewidth = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(~user, scales = "free") +
  labs(
    title = "Nonlinear Rating Growth Models - Actual vs Fitted",
    x = "Game Sequence",
    y = "Rating",
    color = "User"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

ggplotly(p4)
```
